fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The configuration surface (`ee8a`) and the per-run identity (`6cd0`) are both merged, but
nothing reaches the wire: rebar still sends no request headers, so a gateway cannot attribute
or group gate calls. Header values also sit adjacent to `provider_provenance`, written into
verdicts and sidecars (`findings.py:122-123`, `completion_sidecar.py:339`), so delivery without
redaction would put operator-supplied values into durable records.

## Approach

Resolve `${run:...}` references and place the finished headers on the call through pydantic-ai's
`ModelSettings.extra_headers`, by extending the dict returned from `build_model_settings`
(`structured_run.py:338`), whose result flows to the model call at `runner.py:567`.

That seam rather than the transport: one insertion covers every provider supporting the field,
whereas patching transport needs edits at both `providers.py:295` and `anthropic_model.py:155`
and still misses non-httpx providers. `build_model_settings` is already a pure function with a
purity test (`tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py`). Headers are inert on Bedrock at the
pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.2 (`models/bedrock.py` references `extra_headers` zero times); the
`base_url` gate already excludes that path and the docs ticket records it.

**Pass a fresh `dict(...)` per call, never the config-held mapping.** At the pin, the Chat
Completions path reads `model_settings.get('extra_headers', {})` with NO copy
(`models/openai.py:1001`) then `.setdefault('User-Agent', ...)` (`:1002`), mutating the caller's
dict — unlike the Responses path (`:2300`) and `models/anthropic.py:772`, which copy first.
Verified live: a supplied `{"x-corp-tag": "rebar"}` came back carrying `User-Agent`. This is
upstream issue 6866, fixed by PR 6868 after this pin, so the copy is the same remedy upstream
landed. Handing over the config's own dict would pollute it across calls and leak a pydantic-ai
version string into the recorded header-name set, making a signed verdict's provenance
non-deterministic. This is the exact path `base_url` selects.

Headers attach only when `cfg.base_url` is set — a configured intermediary is the only topology
in which they mean anything (verified inert against `api.anthropic.com`), and gating stops an
operator's internal values reaching a public provider. This reuses the condition
`capabilities.py:554` already treats as "an intermediary is present".

**An absent `${run:...}` substituend omits the whole header.** Only two scopes mint an identity
(`gate_dispatch.py`'s two boundaries). `review-code` opens no `gate_config` scope and has no
ticket, so those values are absent there, as for any standalone op. Such a header is dropped
rather than sent empty: an empty correlation header pollutes the gateway, and raising would
break every standalone op merely because headers are configured globally — observability must
never break an operation, the rule `tracing.py` already follows. Deliberately asymmetric with
the unset-`${env:VAR}` hard error: an env var is knowable at config time, so its absence is an
operator mistake, whereas a run value's absence is legitimate runtime context.

Validation is re-applied after `${run:...}` substitution: those references resolve at call time,
so a value that passed config validation is not yet proven safe. Re-running the same name/value
checks closes the validate-before-substitute gap on this second seam.

Redaction: header names are recorded, values never. `provider_provenance` gains at most the
sorted list of configured header names; every log and diagnostic path renders values as a fixed
placeholder.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — add `extra_headers` to the assembled model settings.
- `src/rebar/llm/headers.py` — `${run:...}` resolution against the run identity.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — record header names, never values, in provenance.
- `tests/unit/test_header_delivery.py` (new) — the tests below.

## Testing

Tier: a contract test driving the real assembly seam and capturing what it hands the boundary,
plus in-process unit tests for resolution. The correlation assertion must capture headers from
the real call site — the dict `build_model_settings` actually returns — rather than recomposing
the resolution helpers, because a re-derived oracle stays green if the call site later stops
calling them, which is the only regression it exists to catch.

- Happy path: with `base_url` and a `${run:trace_id}` header configured, the returned settings
  carry the resolved value.
- Edge: with no `base_url`, no `extra_headers` key; with no headers configured, the dict is
  byte-identical to today's.
- Failure: an unknown `${run:bogus}` raises naming the key; a value that only becomes unsafe
  after substitution is rejected.
- Omission: a header carrying `${run:...}` is absent outside a gate run while a sibling literal
  header is still present.
- Redaction: a sentinel value is absent from captured logs and from serialized
  `provider_provenance`, while its header name is present.
- Real-request paths: the non-mutation and merge-precedence criteria cannot be proven from
  `build_model_settings`' return value — both drive a model call through the
  `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport` intercept the epic's spike already used, asserting on the headers
  the transport observed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `base_url` set and headers configured, the dict returned by `build_model_settings`
      contains `extra_headers` with resolved values; checked by calling the real function inside
      a gate-run scope and asserting on its return value, not on recomposed helpers.
- [ ] Every call in one gate run carries the same `${run:trace_id}` value and two runs differ.
- [ ] With `base_url` unset, no `extra_headers` key is present.
- [ ] With no headers configured, the returned dict equals the dict produced before this change.
- [ ] A header carrying `${run:...}` is omitted entirely outside a gate run rather than sent
      empty, while a sibling literal header is still present.
- [ ] An unknown `${run:...}` key raises `LLMConfigError` naming the offending key.
- [ ] A header whose value only becomes unsafe after `${run:...}` substitution is rejected;
      checked by forcing a run value containing CR, LF or NUL.
- [ ] The configured headers mapping is not mutated by a model call; checked against the
      `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport` intercept, which fails against the pinned upstream no-copy path
      if the copy is dropped.
- [ ] A configured header overrides a same-named client default rather than being dropped;
      checked on the intercepted request, pinning the merge precedence that is the
      most-regressed behaviour in comparable projects.
- [ ] A sentinel header value appears in no log record and in no serialized
      `provider_provenance`, while the header name does appear.
